kernels.l1: Trace back from two cubbies at once and you get the two groups of children put together.
kernels.l2: If you trace back from two arrowheads together, you get the same children as tracing back from each one and joining the answers.
kernels.l3: Tracing back respects the hoops: the pre-image of a union is the union of the pre-images, and the same holds for intersections and for outsides.
kernels.l4: f⁻¹(U ∪ V) = f⁻¹(U) ∪ f⁻¹(V), and likewise for ∩ and complement. Every proof pivots on the single equivalence x ∈ f⁻¹(U) ⇔ f(x) ∈ U.
kernels.l5: Pre-image commutes with all the Boolean set operations, and each proof reduces to the pivot equivalence x ∈ f⁻¹(U) ⇔ f(x) ∈ U.
kernels.l6: The pre-image operator is a Boolean homomorphism P(T) → P(S); the direct image is not, which is the asymmetry worth remembering.
kernels.l7: Pre-image commutes with union, intersection, and complement, each proof turning on x ∈ f⁻¹(U) ⇔ f(x) ∈ U. Direct image commutes only with union.
kernels.l8: f⁻¹ is a Boolean algebra homomorphism P(T) → P(S) and sits between the two image operators as an adjoint; this is why continuity is stated with pre-images.
